name: eta_a
description: field application efficiency, the same for all terminals
source: Nominal and lower bound: Awan U.K., Tischbein B., Martius C. (2013) Irrig. Sci. 31, 793-806, doi:10.1007/s00271-012-0362-0, p. 798: average field application ratio 0.43, range 0.37-0.47 for silt loam and silty clay loam soils (Shomakhulum WUA, Khorezm). Upper bound: Tischbein B. et al. (2012) in: Cotton, Water, Salts and Soums, Springer, 69-92, doi:10.1007/978-94-007-1963-7_5, p. 77: application efficiency of 50% in an 850-ha sub-unit in Khorezm (field observations 40-50%, p. 75). The FAO indicative value of 60% for surface irrigation (Brouwer, Prins, Heibloem 1989, Training manual no. 4, Annex I, Table 8) and the improved-practice targets of 0.65-0.67 (Tischbein B. et al. (2012) in: Cotton, Water, Salts and Soums, Springer, 69-92, doi:10.1007/978-94-007-1963-7_5, p. 87; Awan U.K., Tischbein B., Martius C. (2013) Irrig. Sci. 31, 793-806, doi:10.1007/s00271-012-0362-0, p. 800) lie above the current-conditions range.

name: edge_loss_rel_halfwidth
description: relative half-width of the uniform uncertainty of every edge loss fraction 1 - eta_e; the nominal eta_e comes from the dataset or the short-edge rule
source: Of the order of the spread of conveyance efficiencies reported in the reviewed studies: 51% (Gilsha Bai E.B., Rema K.P., Joseph A., Sathian K.K. (2023) JAEI 60, 74-85, doi:10.52151/jae2023601.1798) and 74% (Melsse D.W., Tegegne M.A., Ayele T.M. (2025) Appl. Water Sci. 15, 300, doi:10.1007/s13201-025-02659-z), i.e. losses of 0.26-0.49, about +/-31% around their midpoint. Ponding tests in Khorezm gave losses of about 5% of the discharge per 100 m in small canals of low hierarchy and much lower losses in larger canals (Tischbein B. et al. (2012) in: Cotton, Water, Salts and Soums, Springer, 69-92, doi:10.1007/978-94-007-1963-7_5, p. 86).

name: phi_E
description: share of edge losses that evaporates from the canal water surface (consumed)
source: Awan U.K., Tischbein B., Martius C. (2013) Irrig. Sci. 31, 793-806, doi:10.1007/s00271-012-0362-0, p. 798: about 3% of the irrigation losses evaporate, about 7% go directly to the drains as operational losses and 90% recharge the aquifer (lower Amu Darya, Khorezm). The partition is given there for total losses; it is applied here to canal losses. Range assumed.

name: phi_O
description: share of edge losses that leaves as operational spills
source: Awan U.K., Tischbein B., Martius C. (2013) Irrig. Sci. 31, 793-806, doi:10.1007/s00271-012-0362-0, p. 798: about 7% of the irrigation losses go directly to the drains as operational losses. Range assumed, because operational losses are hard to quantify (Tischbein B. et al. (2012) in: Cotton, Water, Salts and Soums, Springer, 69-92, doi:10.1007/978-94-007-1963-7_5, p. 87).

name: rho_S
description: fraction of canal seepage that is recoverable within the basin
source: No study quantifies the recoverable fraction for the lower Amu Darya. Context: drainage outflow is 55-67% of the irrigation input (Tischbein B. et al. (2012) in: Cotton, Water, Salts and Soums, Springer, 69-92, doi:10.1007/978-94-007-1963-7_5, pp. 76 and 85; Conrad C. et al. (2013) Phys. Chem. Earth 61-62, 52-62, doi:10.1016/j.pce.2013.05.002, p. 59); re-use of drainage water is limited by its salinity of 2.0-2.5 g/l (Conrad C. et al. (2013) Phys. Chem. Earth 61-62, 52-62, doi:10.1016/j.pce.2013.05.002, p. 59); capillary rise from shallow groundwater supplies 16-33% of crop evapotranspiration (Awan U.K., Tischbein B., Martius C. (2013) Irrig. Sci. 31, 793-806, doi:10.1007/s00271-012-0362-0, p. 800; Awan U.K., Tischbein B., Martius C. (2014) Irrig. Sci. 32, 449-458, doi:10.1007/s00271-014-0441-5, p. 457; Tischbein B. et al. (2012) in: Cotton, Water, Salts and Soums, Springer, 69-92, doi:10.1007/978-94-007-1963-7_5, p. 85). The full admissible range is therefore kept, with its midpoint as the nominal value.
